predatory_subset.explanation: These four are the ones a resident meets in person: being harassed, hit, pickpocketed or mugged. Separating them from the rest tells 'busy' apart from 'dangerous' — a place full of shoplifting and vehicle crime is commercial, not threatening to someone walking home.

top_anchors.anchor: On or near White Lion Street

anchor_dispersion.reading: The top five anchors hold 69% of everything. Crime here clusters at a few nodes rather than spreading along the streets.

anchor_caveat: 'On or near X' is an anonymised snap point, not an address. Two incidents on the same anchor may be a hundred metres apart.

sensitivity.explanation: The same box re-fetched with the centre moved 20 m north, south, east and west. A big spread means the number is an artefact of where you put the pin, usually because one anonymised anchor sits just inside or just outside the edge. A small spread means the count is robust.

method: data.police.uk street-level all-crime over a 300 m x 300 m box (half-width 150 m, cosine-corrected), months 2026-01 to 2026-06, 6 of 6 months actually returned. Totals cover the months fetched only — nothing is scaled up to fill a gap. Caveats: locations are anonymised snap points ('On or near X'), there is no night/day split, there is no population or footfall denominator so busy places out-count dangerous ones, and publication runs 2-3 months behind, so this describes a window that has already closed.
